harbor_p08_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_001.text: The permit office stood behind the boat market, where the air smelled of damp reeds instead of salt. Yue had passed it several times without entering. On the tenth week's first inquiry morning, He Ming stopped at its door and asked whether she would have to explain her whole family again. The review clerk said the relevant account concerned where she lodged during the hiring period and what she paid. She could keep other history private. The woman entered carrying one old receipt, relieved and suspicious of how small the question sounded.

harbor_p08_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_002.text: Zeng Kai arrived with his polished stick and an assistant carrying the yard books. The former hiring clerk's witnessed reply was already in the file, linked to the copies he had been permitted to examine. The reviewer, Guo Shanshan, explained the posted charter and questions. She could decide permit corrections and unauthorized verification charges within that authority. Criminal intent, unrelated rental disputes and general damages belonged elsewhere. Yue sat with the inquiry observers. The room lacked the commercial hearing's smell of wet wool, but its chairs were equally determined to make long waiting uncomfortable.

harbor_p08_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_003.text: The first comparison concerned the lodging status yard housed. Individual slips showed addresses outside the yard. The retained bed-charge book showed no corresponding stay for several named workers. Zeng said the phrase meant the yard managed their hiring, not that they slept there. Guo showed the form instruction in force then. It described actual accommodation, with a separate field for hiring office. The owner admitted using a phrase broader than that definition. He wanted the error called customary shorthand. The reviewer asked whose custom and what authority changed the form's meaning.

harbor_p08_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_004.text: The former clerk's letter said the owner directed the batch address method to speed departure. It included a copy of the instruction he retained. Zeng's initials appeared beside the sentence, and he acknowledged them. Individual lodging slips were to follow in an office packet. The packet's transfer error had later delayed access to those slips. Guo distinguished the misleading starting status from the later misroute. Neither became the other person's complete responsibility by being linked. Han Pei watched from the witness chair, seeing where the record she inherited had begun to lose its ordinary meaning.

harbor_p08_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_005.text: Zeng asked why workers did not correct the address at once if it was wrong. He Ming said she thought the yard line meant the place a foreman could find her. Guo asked whether the hiring question made clear it sought a sleeping address. The blank form did; the oral account did not. The former clerk admitted asking where workers were attached for the voyage. That question naturally gathered work points. Guo recorded the mismatch without declaring every worker incapable of understanding a form. The office had asked one thing and entered an answer as another.

harbor_p08_006.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p08_006.text: I slept in a rented room and rested at the yard between night shifts. If someone asked where I belonged for packing, I named the yard. I did not give it permission to become my mother's address, my brother's lodging, or a reason an office should call our household unclaimed. I can show the room receipt for the relevant dates. I will not bring every letter Mother wrote to prove I had a life elsewhere. The question should have been clear enough that my ordinary answer did not have to defend all of that afterward.

harbor_p08_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_007.text: The room receipt matched the relevant period. Guo permitted an extract of dates and lodging point, keeping unrelated charges outside the public summary. Other workers supplied similar bounded sources through agreed routes. One had slept at the yard for four nights and then moved. His actual dates required a mixed entry, not a wholesale outside-yard correction. Yue liked that the review could preserve an inconvenient exception. A sound account was not the list that made Zeng look worst. It was the one a person could use to find where someone actually was during the period asked.

harbor_p08_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_008.text: The second question concerned verification money. The yard book showed twenty-nine workers charged three copper each, totaling eighty-seven. Harbor receipts showed twenty-nine public permit copper remitted, one per worker. The remaining fifty-eight stayed in the yard account under registration service. The charter allowed an additional service charge only through an informed separate agreement, not an implied condition of getting hired. Zeng produced no such agreements for these twenty-nine. He said the office work had real costs. Guo agreed that work could cost money and asked for the authority to make these workers pay it.

harbor_p08_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_009.text: He Ming recognized her three-copper entry. She had paid from earlier savings at the hiring counter, separately from the later six-copper wage advance. The public one-copper portion was not disputed. The extra two had been described as necessary verification. Her wage claim had never included this separate money. She put her old receipt beside the book reference and looked furious at finding another ordinary loss she had accepted. Yue knew better than to celebrate a new question simply because it could now be proved. Proof did not give back the months when the small amount mattered.

harbor_p08_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_010.text: Zeng's assistant supplied the printed fee notice the yard used. It listed three copper for shore verification, without separating the public permit from an optional service. The posted harbor rule had been delivered to the yard before the batch instruction, with a signed receipt. Zeng acknowledged receiving it and said he believed his office service qualified. Guo asked where workers had been told they could refuse that service while retaining ordinary hiring access. The notice contained no such route. His belief did not replace an agreement the rule expressly required.

harbor_p08_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_011.text: The former clerk's response confirmed he collected the three because the owner directed it. He kept one-copper public remittance references and entered two as yard service. He did not seek separate worker consent, believing the posted yard notice was sufficient. Guo compared that account with the signed instruction and receipts. It established an unauthorized charge method and particular acts. The record did not need a claim that every person at the yard intended to erase households. Han Pei listened, then recognized how the same failure made fees look inevitable and addresses look settled.

harbor_p08_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_012.text: The owner blamed clerical practice for turning his intention into a rigid charge. His initials sat beside the words collect three at registration. Guo asked what exception he had authorized. He named none. The former clerk's practice matched that instruction. Zeng could question other parts of the letter, but this act had corroborating sources and his admission of the mark. His stick began tapping again. The reviewer waited until it stopped before asking whether he had any additional source. The silence was unpleasant enough to keep everyone attentive without becoming a verdict of itself.

harbor_p08_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_013.text: Guo gave a preliminary finding that the public twenty-nine copper was properly remitted and the extra fifty-eight lacked the required agreements. The yard had to refund two to each of the twenty-nine identified payers through the charter's correction process, subject to the stated review. The initial wage total remained six hundred forty-two, already paid. Refunds were separate charges returned, not a new wage calculation. The recipient schedule would preserve current contact and authority questions. An unidentified new claimant would require evidence rather than receive two merely for appearing at the counter.

harbor_p08_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_014.text: Zeng said fifty-eight copper would damage his present business. Guo asked for any lawful installment proposal that preserved the refund obligations and protected recipients from further delay. He consulted his assistant, then agreed to place fifty-eight from the yard's own business account into the permit office's separate refund custody. He preferred closing the defined obligation to repeated visits. The keeper supplied a receipt before accepting funds. Qin's closed guarantee box was not reopened. The source and purpose would stay visible even if the same harbor building held both records.

harbor_p08_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_015.text: The review also required correction of supported lodging-status entries and a public explanation of the batch method's limits. It referred any broader claimed loss or disputed intent to the proper route with preserved evidence. Zeng could seek review of the findings without withholding the accepted refund deposit. His assistant wanted wording that said the yard regretted confusion. Guo required the notice to say unauthorized extra charges and incorrect lodging statuses, describing supported acts rather than offering a mood. The owner disliked the words because they gave people a reason to ask what happened next.

harbor_p08_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_016.text: Han Pei gave her own account of the public unclaimed heading. She used the inherited term for unresolved recipients and expected claimants to correct missing information at the desk. The original heading did not explain that the list proved neither abandonment nor death. She had since added that clarification with a dated history. Guo examined whether a further notice or process correction was appropriate. Han did not ask the owner to carry responsibility for her choice simply because his source error preceded it. Yue watched her read the sentence steadily, proud and worried for her friend at once.

harbor_p08_017.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p08_017.text: I want the record to say what the desk knew and what it did with that knowledge. We knew the thirteen references were unresolved, not that thirteen households had vanished. I chose the heading because it belonged to our forms and because I was trying to prevent a premature bond return. The intention did not make the public meaning clear. I have corrected the notice. I still need a method that asks a usable question before a person has spent six days proving the office should have asked it differently. That work cannot end with my regret.

harbor_p08_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_018.text: Guo asked the administrator to review the contact procedure within ordinary authority, using Han's account and claimant examples. She could order the current record corrected but could not create permanent staffing from a hearing sentence. The administrator would answer with an allocation or a stated limitation at the term review. Han accepted the distinction and asked for the review date in writing. He Ming watched her insist on a date with the same impatience she had once brought to Han's window. Afterward, she told Yue the clerk sounded almost like a claimant. Yue said she was one for that question.

harbor_p08_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_019.text: The first day's session ended before the corrected schedules were ready. Zeng left with his assistant and no audience for a speech at the door. He Ming went to her packing shift, carrying proof of a two-copper refund due. Yue's paid inquiry half-day ended at the office. She returned the board and walked to the harbor wall alone. The water had the dull shine of pewter under a cloud. She remembered how many people called a small sum insignificant until they had to lose it. Fifty-eight was large to the yard; two could still be large to each worker.

harbor_p08_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_020.text: At the repair shed, the keeper's boy found her looking at the window and asked whether someone had lost a boat. She said someone had collected money wrongly and would return it. He asked whether she was happy. She said a little, and angry it happened. He considered that, then offered her the last sweet cake because two feelings probably required more supper. Yue bought him another the following day instead of turning his gift into a lesson about balance. His ordinary generosity had reached a place the hearing's correct words did not touch.

harbor_p08_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_021.text: He Ming received her two-copper refund among the first direct collections. She checked the receipt carefully and bought nothing with the money that afternoon. She wanted to hold it without immediately translating it into food or rent. The amount came from the separately deposited yard refund, not the merchant's returned guarantee. Han Pei watched the collection from her own desk duty and asked whether the form was clear. He Ming said yes. Then she said she would prefer never learning that much about receipts. The clerk laughed because the feeling belonged to both of them.

harbor_p08_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_022.text: Twenty-three identified payers completed direct or authorized collections during the week, receiving forty-six copper in total. Six refund entries remained, twelve copper held for their lawful recipients under dated contact routes and review points. The fifty-eight-copper yard deposit therefore stood as forty-six paid and twelve still held. No clerk called the retained portion spare money. Some workers had left the harbor before the review. The office would use permitted contact routes rather than publish private locations or assume refusal. Yue noted the actual state in the public aggregate, resisting an attractive sentence saying all refunds were complete.

harbor_p08_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_023.text: The language desk arranged a bounded hour for two payers who needed the findings explained in their own speech. Yue's inquiry appointment covered relevant outreach, and Han approved its six-copper charge before the session. Interpretation expenses rose from six to twelve, leaving twelve within the original twenty-four ceiling. The interpreter read the specific refund, contact correction and review rights, checking questions rather than making assent sound smooth. One worker disagreed with the stated old lodging point. The desk recorded the disagreement for source correction. Understanding a payment did not require approving every line around it.

harbor_p08_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_024.text: That worker, Rao E, had moved twice during the hiring period. The retained slip named only the first room. A landlord receipt established the second. Guo's clerk corrected the dates through the documented route without treating Rao as a new fraud problem. The man said he had feared asking because each change seemed to make him look less reliable. The interpreter preserved that concern in the feedback note only with his permission. Yue heard it and thought about how a life lived between rooms could seem disorderly mainly to a form demanding one address before it would allow a wage.

harbor_p08_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_025.text: The approved public findings and correction forms required additional copies for collection points. The inquiry paid four copper in authorized paper and preparation, taking copying use from six to ten and leaving fourteen of its twenty-four ceiling. The office's ordinary staff made and checked the schedules under their own funded duties. Yue used one paid half-day to compare references for the households linked to her inquiry. She did not inspect unrelated private permit packets. By the end of the tenth week she would have twenty completed inquiry half-days, with four remaining before the initial term closed.

harbor_p08_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_026.text: Zeng returned to inspect the refund schedule with his assistant. He asked whether missing recipients would let him recover the twelve immediately. The keeper showed the charter's hold, contact and review conditions. His deposit existed to refund identified unauthorized charges, not to become a bet on whether workers could be found quickly. Any eventual return decision would need its own permitted basis and notice. He asked for copies and received the relevant pages. Yue saw him counting the six names under his breath, making the same people visible whom the batch address had once made convenient to overlook.

harbor_p08_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_027.text: Outside, the yard owner told He Ming she had made a small matter expensive. She replied that he could have charged one instead of three. He said the yard did work for people. She said work needed an agreed price. Their short exchange threatened to become a familiar long quarrel. Yue did not step between them as a superior envoy. The clerk called them back to collect their papers, and both complied. He Ming later admitted she had wanted to say something much crueller. Keeping it unsaid had cost effort she did not want mistaken for gratitude.

harbor_p08_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_028.text: The former hiring clerk sent another letter after receiving the preliminary comparison. He accepted the record of collecting three and using the batch address under Zeng's instruction. He asked that his current employer not receive unrelated private worker records with any referral. The permit office preserved necessary findings and protected irrelevant information through the applicable route. The letter included a personal apology he allowed He Ming to read. She read it once and put it down. She could accept that he wished he had done better without promising to forgive on the day the page arrived.

harbor_p08_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_029.text: Han's own correction notice used the words open wage inquiries instead of unclaimed households. It described the historic problem and current result without erasing the first posting. The administrator approved a short explanation at the collection points and a review of how future contact questions began. Han signed the version she wrote. Yue helped fasten it under the existing record reference. Fen read it during a copying errand and said it would have spared her one frightening morning. The clerk thanked her. The comment mattered more than praise because it named an actual day she could no longer repair.

harbor_p08_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_030.text: Fen delivered clean copies to the tea seller's collection point under her shop's paid task, not as an unpaid extension of Yue's inquiry. The seller inspected the heading and said she finally understood why the wage money and the household search had separate slips. Fen explained it with an example from her father's chest, then stopped before turning a delivery into a lecture. The seller paid the agreed shop fee and offered tea. Fen accepted the tea as a small gift she could decline, pleased that ordinary work had begun to bring ordinary exchanges after so many desperate requests.

harbor_p08_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_031.text: Luo Jian spent that evening teaching Fen a knot she did not actually need for copying. She indulged him until he tried to call the lesson an essential harbor skill. Then she made him practice a character with three turns he always muddled. Each became a patient instructor for roughly two minutes. After that, they criticized the other's hand position and laughed. His injured fingers tired sooner, so they stopped. Fen did not treat the pause as defeat. The clinician's limits had become part of their evening instead of a reason every conversation had to begin with fear.

harbor_p08_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_032.text: Dai Min came to collect her own two-copper permit refund. Her husband had not been among those charged in that batch, so no new estate question appeared merely because they shared a household. She showed her hiring receipt and made her own mark. He Ming waited outside with a net sample. They went to the seller together, discussing the next order's rate. The widow's ordinary independence pleased Yue, though she had no reason to announce it to anyone. Dai needed payment and work more than a story in which others admired her for surviving a difficult month.

harbor_p08_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_033.text: Miao received the public permit findings because his employer's voyage records had used the shortened addresses. He asked whether the yard's fifty-eight should reduce the earlier wage draw. Han showed the accounts: permit charges were separate private money, wages already earned and paid were unchanged. He understood after seeing He Ming's fee receipt outside her wage payment history. He said it was remarkable how many kinds of money could share one person's hand without paying the same debt. The clerk smiled at his awkward description. It was more accurate than several impressive arguments he made during his first week.

harbor_p08_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_034.text: The merchant's fixed agency fee reached Miao under his own employment term. He counted it at the shore yard and paid the storeman an overdue small expense they had disputed. The lost bonus remained lost. Qian's message advised him to keep future claims under control. Miao folded it and asked the clerk about neutral wage-recipient notices for the next voyage. Yue heard the request while returning her inquiry board. He had not become a worker delegate. He had begun seeing that information kept under control could create costs his employer later expected him to explain.

harbor_p08_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_035.text: Yan Su asked He Ming whether she would join a short paid discussion about work-line reporting through the ordinary port consultation budget. She asked for the time and rate before agreeing. He grinned and said the office had taught her something tiresome. She answered that the yard taught her first. The discussion would hear actual worker examples and propose a safe stop route, not replace technical training with opinions. Bo attended during his assigned paid hours and looked nervous beside older packers. He Ming asked him which threat most often made people keep quiet. He supplied a concrete example.

harbor_p08_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_036.text: The example concerned a hiring foreman who threatened to skip the next shift if a worker interrupted a late load. The report had a date and named people willing to answer, but the port clerk would seek their accounts before deciding. Yan did not promise instant punishment. He offered a current clear stop instruction in his own lane and a route to report retaliation. Bo said that helped only where Yan stood. The foreman accepted the limit and proposed another responsible contact when he was absent. The consultation became useful precisely where its first attractive answer proved incomplete.

harbor_p08_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_037.text: Yue spent a free afternoon at Duan's painting yard with Han. The clerk had arranged a beginner session, paying its charge. She kept her job and asked for a time that fitted her roster. Duan taught her to draw a curve along a hull seam without fighting the grain. Han wanted the brush to behave like a pen. It did not. Yue watched her irritation become concentration. The lesson had no responsibility to repair the harbor. Its value lay partly in giving Han a place where being new was permitted and mistakes stained a scrap instead of a claimant's week.

harbor_p08_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_038.text: Walking back, Han said she had feared other clerks would think painting frivolous after the permit hearing. Yue asked whether shame required every free hour to resemble penance. Han looked annoyed at being understood too quickly. She had made a harmful heading and would answer for it. That did not give the office ownership of her whole life. She said the thought felt selfish. Yue said perhaps it would feel less so after a few ordinary evenings. They bought a cabbage and argued about who had cooked the last one badly, a subject on which shame could safely become ridiculous.

harbor_p08_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_039.text: At the shed, the boy discovered the kite's tail had tangled around its own patched fin. He blamed Fen's legal advice. Fen said the fish failed to read flight conditions. Luo tried to untie it one-handed until they reminded him scissors existed. The boy refused cutting because he wanted the same tail. Yue found the knot's loose end with her ordinary fingers and worked it free. Nobody expected luminous arms to improve that task. The kite rose the next day with every fin intact, its ambition to own the sea now accompanied by a modest ability to leave the roof.

harbor_p08_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_040.text: He Ming's plant leaned toward the window and shed one leaf. She accused it of complaining about lodging. Han said it needed less water. Qin's gardener agreed after seeing the wet soil. The woman moved it to a brighter place and laughed at how quickly care became insistence that the cared-for thing accept her method. He Jun, present for supper, looked as though he wanted to make a personal analogy. She warned him not to. He obeyed, then passed the kettle. Their restraint made Yue laugh before either sibling could begin another quarrel about who understood the lesson.

harbor_p08_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_041.text: The permit keeper sent contact notices for the six remaining refunds through named collection routes. One address came back obsolete. The office retained its twelve-copper balance while seeking current safe contact from the relevant keeper. It did not advertise a person's private location or make every neighbor a recipient. Yue could assist the households linked to her inquiry within scheduled shifts, but the refund administration had its own assigned clerk. A corrected result needed people after the hearing as much as during it. The keeper entered the next review date before opening a different ordinary account.

harbor_p08_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_042.text: One former worker answered from a canal repair village, authorizing a specific collection route for his two copper. The clerk verified the authority and arranged the permitted delivery. The actual refund total rose to forty-eight, leaving ten held for five payers. The office did not spend more than two to deliver two without checking the approved ordinary route; the worker could receive it alongside an existing scheduled transfer. Yue read the aggregate update and admired the modest efficiency. Finding people deserved effort, but a remedy also needed a practical way to reach them without inventing expense beneath a tiny sum.

harbor_p08_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_043.text: Another payer sent a furious message asking why a two-copper refund took longer than the original three-copper collection. The permit clerk answered with the specific identity and route question, preserving the first contact date. He Ming read the public feedback with sympathy. She suggested that the finding notice should identify the collection task in the first sentence. Han agreed and asked the administrator for authority to revise the current route form. The proposal was ordinary enough to be overlooked. They kept it visible by naming the source example and the person responsible for deciding it.

harbor_p08_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_044.text: Sui Yan's cargo quarantine finally reached its closing technical conditions. Cleared goods had dispositions, spoiled material had licensed disposal records, sample findings were preserved, and access hazards had moved into the vessel's separate repair authority. She signed closure within her license, identifying what it did and did not certify. The Salt Lantern still required seaworthiness approval before departure. The captain walked the empty work face with an assistant and let him check the last tag. The berth looked larger without clustered claimants. Its space brought relief, and a sudden loneliness she did not expect to admit.

harbor_p08_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_045.text: Yue met her afterward carrying a jar of onion relish from He Ming. The captain said people would remember only how long the vessel stayed. Yue said some would remember receiving coats or learning where a father slept. Sui smiled, then said those were not her findings. Yue agreed. They could still belong to the town's account of the same weeks. The captain opened the relish and found it sharper than she expected. He Ming had warned her, which she ignored. She laughed at that ordinary failure of notice and saved the rest for supper.

harbor_p08_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_046.text: Yan Su escorted the last loaned handling item back to maintenance custody. The temporary frame returned earlier; now the spare rated sling and boundary posts were checked off after cleaning and inspection. The department retained its equipment and next-use duties. Yue acquired none of it. The foreman asked what she would do after the inquiry term. She said she was deciding. He said good, because unfinished work would happily make that decision for her if permitted. She disliked the accuracy. He offered no advice about where to go, only a reminder that his own lane had work before she came.

harbor_p08_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_047.text: Deren's independent review sent another request about earlier platform inspection dates. He had kept a personal notebook with shift marks, though it did not establish what each inspection included. He allowed a relevant extract and kept private spending pages covered. The review compared the dates with the official routine. Yan answered without asking the injured man to soften his claim. Their friendship had become less comfortable and more durable. Deren still wanted lost-work compensation. He also wanted Yan to know that supplying the notebook was not a declaration they could never joke together again.

harbor_p08_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_048.text: The men joked together that afternoon when Bo counted the same spare hook twice. Deren asked whether the second count earned another wage. Yan said it earned a fresh count by someone paying attention. Bo groaned and corrected the stock list. Yue watched from the dry visitor line, pleased that humor could survive an unresolved responsibility question. It did not settle the question or make injury support unnecessary. It gave the people involved ordinary air to breathe between letters, records and tasks. She thought a town needed that air as much as clear words on a notice board.

harbor_p08_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_049.text: The tenth week's second paid inquiry shift put Yue beside Han to prepare term-review evidence. Twenty half-days were now complete, earning forty of the forty-eight wage copper. Ferry costs remained six, copying ten, interpretation twelve. Their separate ceilings left eighteen, fourteen and twelve. Bed and meals continued at the agreed rate within seventy-two for the term. They checked actual receipts rather than assuming the ceilings had all been spent. The unspent lines could not become a personal bonus or another project's purse. Yue wrote the remaining four shifts in her calendar before listing the tasks they could realistically contain.

harbor_p08_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_050.text: The administrator asked for a proposal on future contact work before the twelfth-week closure. Han wanted a staffed place for long questions. He Ming wanted outreach that found people unable to spend a morning at the desk. Sui wanted clear distinctions among passenger contact, cargo and wages. Yan wanted a work-line report route. Yue said a bounded term could test some of these without promising permanent coverage. The administrator asked for choices, not a list pretending all could be free. They agreed to bring costs and responsible people to the next meeting rather than use friendship as the hidden workforce.

harbor_p08_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_051.text: He Ming disliked the proposal's word test. Families were not experimental slips, she said. Han answered that a new method needed checking so its failures did not become invisible custom. The conversation nearly returned to their first week's accusation. Yue asked for one concrete difference they wanted within the proposed term. He Ming wanted someone who could not attend to receive a clear relevant answer. Han wanted that task assigned and paid. The two hopes fitted together once they described a person and an hour instead of defending a word. They both looked mildly annoyed at how simple it sounded.

harbor_p08_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_052.text: Miao brought a next-voyage draft to the wage clerk for the public procedure reference. It used individual lodging questions and separate safe-contact choices. He had no authority to impose a harbor form, but he could make the employer's paperwork less misleading. Han supplied the current public instructions and asked him not to present them as approval of every contract term. He accepted the reference. Yue noticed the agent was no longer carrying only documents designed to release money. Some now sought to prevent a problem before it became an expensive story attached to his own signed note.

harbor_p08_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_053.text: Zeng's assistant sent confirmation that the yard fee notice had been removed and replaced with the lawful public amount plus a separately offered service requiring agreement. Guo's office would inspect the new practice within its normal authority. The owner's compliance did not erase fifty-eight owed or the historical status correction. The remaining refund balance stood at ten after twenty-four payments. He Ming kept her two copper in a little separate wrap until she finally spent one on thread. Returning money had restored choice, including the choice to use it for something so ordinary the yard would never notice.

harbor_p08_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_054.text: The former clerk's apology remained on He Ming's shelf beside Mother's letter. She did not reread it often. One evening, she decided to answer with the facts she wanted him to know: she accepted the corrected record, received her refund, and hoped he would ask the sleeping-address question properly next time. She offered no grand forgiveness. Yue helped spell one word only when asked. The letter went through ordinary paid postage from He Ming's purse. Its smallness pleased her. She could respond without making another person's peace the whole measure of what the weeks cost her.

harbor_p08_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_055.text: Han received notice that her current supervisor accepted the public-heading correction and required future list scope to be explained plainly. It was an administrative instruction, not a criminal judgment or a promise she would never make another error. She placed it in the office record and went to her painting lesson on her arranged free evening. Yue watched her leave with a brush wrapped in scrap cloth she owned. The small possession would stay with Han, whose life belonged here. Yue felt glad and sad that a friendship could grow roots in a place where her own pack remained ready.

harbor_p08_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_056.text: Fen's first regular copying week ended with pay she checked against the agreed shifts. Luo asked whether she wanted him to hold the money safely. She said no, then asked him to show her how he wrapped his own purse against rain. He did. Accepting knowledge was easier when it did not require surrendering control. At the tea stall, she bought a bowl for them both as a gift from her earnings. Luo thanked her and resisted making a speech about how grown she had become. The silence was his most successful gift to the evening.

harbor_p08_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_057.text: Dai Min invited He Ming to eat at her room after completing a net order. Yue came too by invitation. The comb rested on a shelf without becoming the meal's subject. They talked about thread prices, Fen's copy work and a neighbor's terrible singing. Dai laughed, then wiped her eyes because laughing still surprised her. Nobody explained the feeling. The women passed the dishes and let it belong. Outside, the harbor's bells marked ordinary duty changes. The sound had once divided her husband's last days into unanswered questions. Tonight it mainly told her the rice should come off the stove.

harbor_p08_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_058.text: A message from the canal payer confirmed safe delivery of the two-copper refund. The permit keeper filed it under the original collection authorization. Ten remained held for five people; no new transfer occurred that day. Yue liked the acknowledgment because the route had done what it claimed, and the person did not have to appear merely to make the office comfortable. Han used the example in the term proposal with private details omitted. It showed a task that worked. They also included the obsolete address that had not yet worked, refusing to write only successes into the next plan.

harbor_p08_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_059.text: On her rest day, Yue walked beyond the last warehouse to a strip of shore where no one could hand her a form. She practiced one quiet fourth-stage interval with a light marker and stopped within her established limit. The sea made no sign that cultivation mattered to it. She sat afterward with her ordinary cup and watched a crab disappear beneath a stone. Work had changed how she listened to people. It had not answered where she wanted to stay. She allowed that question to remain hers without assigning a clerk to resolve it before the next tide.

harbor_p08_060.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_060.text: The repair shed keeper asked whether Yue wanted to reserve the room beyond the inquiry term. She said she needed the proposed work agreement first. The keeper offered the actual private rate if she chose to stay without it. Yue wrote the amount in her personal notes. An unanswered future did not prevent a practical comparison. She could afford a short interval from earned wages and savings, but indefinite free help would slowly consume that choice. The keeper respected the answer and promised to give notice before renting the room onward. Neither woman made affection do the work of terms.

harbor_p08_061.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_061.text: The boy flew the repaired kite beside the dry square while Yue watched the line. Han's tiny gull rode the fish badly because the brush mark made its eye look suspicious. Fen said it was investigating ownership. The boy declared the investigation closed when the kite rose above the roofs. A sudden drop brought it back into the square, safely clear of the quay. Luo said the sea had appealed. Everyone laughed. The object remained the boy's ordinary kite. Yue handed back the spool and felt relieved she would not have to carry their shared evenings away in her pack.

harbor_p08_062.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_062.text: The eleventh week's work notice arrived as a creek barge ran aground near the outer reed bank. Its passengers and migrant crew would reach the harbor through the ordinary emergency landing route once the pilot and rescue staff completed safe transfer. The administrator asked the existing desks to prepare contact and wage questions under their normal duties. Yue had four initial inquiry shifts left, not a limitless new commission. She agreed to one scheduled outreach task within scope and asked which clerk would continue afterward. The name was supplied before anybody called the arrivals another list of unclaimed households.

harbor_p08_063.speaker: narrator
harbor_p08_063.text: He Ming saw the grounded barge from the shore path and stopped joking about the kite. Its people were visible against the rail, small figures waiting for an ordinary rescue boat to approach at the safe angle. Yan Su had gone with the trained harbor crew. Sui's office would assess cargo handling only if relevant hazards appeared; the passengers' safe transfer came first. Yue stayed on the shore where the receiving desk assigned her task. The harbor had completed one voyage's claims. Another set of lives was already coming toward its gates, carrying names that would need questions asked better.
